clue.text: Feeling experienced by daughter after broken heart?

indicators.note: after places the daughter's letter behind the reworked heart
something broken is in pieces, so the word heart is to be reassembled in a new order

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A question about what a daughter goes through once her heart has been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' reworks heart into HATRE; 'after' sets D last. The surface suggests grief, but the feeling meant is far harsher.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense loathing is a strong emotion, so it qualifies as a feeling.

clue.text: Nominate a parking issue

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
a point is an issue under discussion

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put forward a parking question.
explanation.definitionFit: To name someone for a post is to nominate them, the same as giving them a role.

clue.text: Promote and congratulate with no pressure

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the pressure letter is removed

parts.note: to praise is to congratulate
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A boss promotes and congratulates a worker without piling on pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes P from PRAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift someone to a higher rank is to elevate or promote them.

clue.text: Current deal, say, that's floating around

parts.note: a drift is a current or flow
deal is pine or fir timber, an example of wood

explanation.surface: A current trade agreement, apparently drifting along aimlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' looks like an agreement, but it is softwood timber.
explanation.definitionFit: This is timber washed by currents that drifts about on the water, so it is floating around.

clue.text: Courage and instinct about politician no one backed

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the instinct word goes round the politician

parts.note: a gut feeling is an instinct
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: backed means the letters for no and one are read in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tribute to someone with nerve and good instincts who stands up to an unpopular politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' and 'backed' are the two signals; 'no one' splits into two words, the second being the Roman numeral, before turning round to make ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumption covers initiative and spirit as well as common sense, and dictionaries give courage among its senses.

clue.text: Fall apart, having won kitty with nothing in

indicators.note: in says the nothing letter goes inside, between the won and kitty words

parts.note: got means obtained or won
a pot is a kitty of money in a game
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A gambler wins the pot but finds nothing in it, and goes to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with nothing in' puts the zero-shaped letter in the middle of the two words, not inside the kitty alone.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means deteriorate or go to ruin, which is to fall apart.

clue.text: Gathers the writer set off

parts.note: the writer, from the setter's view, is me

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer gathers material and sets off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SET into ETS.
explanation.definitionFit: When people assemble for a session they meet, so meets means gathers.

clue.text: Seem upset wearing G-string for such a melody

indicators.note: wearing means being dressed in, so the garment goes round the upset letters

parts.note: a thong is a G-string

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters of seem are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone looks embarrassed in a G-string, as if to a striptease tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' makes EMES from seem; 'wearing' puts the garment round it. The definition leans on the whole surface: such a melody is the kind played at a strip show.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune identifying a film or show is the sort of melody meant here.

clue.text: This will produce a corn if fused

definitions.text: This will produce a corn if fused

parts.words: This will produce a corn if fused
parts.note: fusing the two words a and corn gives the nut from which this grows, and in turn the grown thing yields such nuts

explanation.walkthrough: 'a corn' looks like a grain, but joined up it is the nut this tree bears.
explanation.definitionFit: Acorns are the nuts of the oak, so this tree produces them.

clue.text: New pine kitchen? An awful bore

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material
taken as written as anagram material

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a new pine kitchen and a guest finds the whole thing tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges PINE KITCHEN plus AN; 'New' looks like a plain adjective on the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a thoroughly tiresome, irritating person or thing, which is an awful bore.

clue.text: Avoid putting favourites back on team

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is written after it

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

indicators.note: back means the word for favourites is read in reverse

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in teacher's pets

explanation.surface: A manager dodges an issue by putting favourite players back into the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes STEP from the favourites; 'on' places it after the team word in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To step aside from a question or problem is to evade it, which is to avoid it.

clue.text: Try blocking extremely spurious cuts

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way between, so the trial word goes between the outer letters
extremely points to the extreme letters, first and last, of spurious

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court

explanation.surface: An attempt to stop specious budget cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives S and S from spurious; 'blocking' sets HEAR between them. Try is used in its court sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To shear sheep or hair is to cut it, so the verb form matches cuts.

clue.text: Small flat sort of poker with one ring

parts.note: stud is a variety of poker
I is the Roman numeral for one
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A poker player in a small flat, wearing a single ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small flat' looks like a description, but it is the definition; 'Small' does not give S here.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-room apartment is called a studio flat, so it is a small flat.

clue.text: Bore just netting female insect

parts.note: a drag is a bore, something tedious

indicators.note: netting means catching inside, so the word for just encloses the female letter

parts.note: only means just

explanation.surface: A tedious person just catches a female insect in a net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'netting' places F inside ONLY.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a long-bodied flying insect with two pairs of clear wings.

clue.text: During drinks, got up for flowers

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the rising word sits inside the drinks

parts.note: teas are drinks
rose means got up

explanation.surface: Someone stood up during drinks to fetch some flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' is the container signal: the rising word sits within the drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: These are a class of hybrid garden roses, so they are flowers.

clue.text: Breaking up as a part needed for equipment

indicators.note: breaking means coming apart, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A part is needed when a machine breaks up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' rearranges UP AS A PART.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is the set of tools or machinery for a task, which is equipment.

clue.text: Manxman perhaps needing company to replace is 23

indicators.note: to replace says one letter group takes over from another within the word

parts.note: a Manxman lives on the Isle of Man, so is an example of an islander
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzling sentence about a Manx resident who needs a firm to take his place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' is the substitution signal. The definition is the answer to 23, a sieve. The Isle of Man is an island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is a perforated bowl for draining food, a kind of kitchen sieve.

clue.text: Finished second even without regulars to supervise

parts.note: over means finished

indicators.note: without regulars means dropping every other letter, keeping the first and third of even

explanation.surface: Finishing second without the regular team players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without regulars' removes V and N from even, leaving E and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch over a task and direct it is to oversee it, so it means supervise.

clue.text: Took for granted going topless and continued

indicators.note: going topless means losing its top, the first letter in a down answer

parts.note: presumed means took for granted

explanation.surface: Someone assumed it was fine to sunbathe topless and carried on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' drops the first letter, P, from PRESUMED.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on after a break is to start again, so the past tense means continued.

clue.text: Temple leaving returning sea-dog appalled

indicators.note: returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
leaving means coming out of, so the letters emerge from the words sea-dog appalled

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A horrified old sailor walks away from a temple and heads back.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Temple leaving' as the definition, but then nothing signals the hidden letters: 'leaving' is that signal, and 'returning' then reads ADOGAP backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower temple found in East Asia.

clue.text: Shift editor treated wounds

parts.note: a shift is a loose straight dress

explanation.surface: An editor changed position, or perhaps worked a shift tending injuries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' looks like a verb, but it is a style of dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To apply bandages to a cut is to dress it, so this past tense means treated wounds.

clue.text: Improve behaviour of soldiers with criminal record

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
form is slang for a criminal record

explanation.surface: Soldiers with a criminal past are urged to mend their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a person with previous convictions 'has form'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform is to change for the better, especially in conduct, which is improving behaviour.

clue.text: Friendly final check before end of day

indicators.note: before places the chess word ahead of the letter in a down answer

parts.note: mate, as in checkmate, is the final check in chess

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of day

explanation.surface: A friendly last check before the day finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives Y from day. 'final check' is checkmate in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone matey is sociable and chummy, so the word means friendly.

clue.text: Riddle of second coach

parts.note: a trainer coaches athletes

explanation.surface: A puzzle set by the assistant coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle, but here it is the noun for a coarse sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a large coarse sieve for soil or gravel, a kind of sieve or strainer.

clue.text: Divine liquid from Norwich originally

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A sacred drink said to have come from Norwich long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes letters running across Norwich and originally; 'originally' looks like a first-letter signal but is just cover. Norwich is a city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this is the ethereal fluid flowing in the veins of the gods.

clue.text: Strikers perhaps full of iron with time before games

indicators.note: before places the first part ahead of the games
full of means containing, so the word for perhaps holds the iron and time letters

parts.note: say means perhaps or for example
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
matches are games

explanation.surface: Footballers, perhaps, with iron in their blood and time before games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' is the container signal and 'before' orders the charade. Strikers look like footballers, but these are things you strike.
explanation.definitionFit: These are matches struck to light, so they are strikers, with perhaps marking the example.

clue.text: Action taken about Welsh river estuary ultimately is naive

indicators.note: taken about means wrapped around, so the action word goes round the river letters

parts.note: a deed is an action
the Wye rises in Wales

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of estuary

explanation.surface: Someone takes action around a Welsh estuary, perhaps a little too innocently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives Y from estuary; 'taken about' wraps the action round the river and that Y. The River Wye flows from Wales into England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sentimental and innocent, easily moved, is naive in outlook.

clue.text: Busy editors, ignoring Independent, walked purposefully

indicators.note: busy suggests bustling movement, so the remaining letters are jumbled
ignoring means leaving out, so the letter for Independent is dropped from editors

explanation.surface: Busy editors, snubbing a newspaper, marched off with purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops I from EDITORS; 'Busy' rearranges EDTORS. The Independent is also a British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: This past tense of stride means walked with long, decisive steps.
